# Free-account consumers — the generated enumeration

**Phase 2 · T202a** · session `CC-20261005-r6h2` · generated 2026-10-05

Every file that **reads one of the two columns directly**. Not every file whose behaviour depends
on them — see the limitations below, which name three that depend on them through a helper and are
structurally invisible to this scan.
**Generated by `backend/src/scripts/enumerateFreeAccountConsumers.ts`, not written from memory**,
and pinned by `backend/src/services/__tests__/freeAccountConsumers.test.ts` so a new consumer
arriving later is a failed build rather than a silent behaviour change on a public signup path.

## Why this file exists

Three successive revisions of the Phase 2 plan carried a hand-written list of the consumers that
would move when `enrollment_type` and `tier` start being written together. **It was short every
time.** Audit cycle 1 found one missing consumer, cycle 2 found two more, and a direct count
found **31** non-test files mentioning `enrollment_type` where the plan had named 8 — `git grep -l enrollment_type workstream/growth-os-reset-phase1 -- "backend/src/**/*.ts" | grep -v __tests__ | wc -l`, measured at the phase-1 base. (An earlier draft said 33, counted mid-task with files this phase had just added, so it was reproducible at no commit at all.) A list a human
maintains in prose will be short again the next time someone adds a reader, and the cost of being
short here is an untested behaviour change on the signup path.

## What changes, and for whom

Two populations move, **in opposite directions**, which is why a single "what breaks" list was
never going to work:

| Population | Today | Gains | 
|---|---|---|
| **A — portal free accounts** (`freeSignupService`) | `tier: 'guest'`, `enrollment_type: 'standard'` | **`enrollment_type: 'explorer'`** |
| **B — `/enroll` Explorers** (`createExplorerEnrollment`) | `enrollment_type: 'explorer'`, `tier` left at its `'member'` default | **`tier: 'guest'`** |

## How a file is classified

- **BRANCHING** — the code compares a column to a literal or filters a query by one, so its
  *output can flip*. Needs a behaviour test in T202b.
- **REPORTING** — it selects, returns or displays the value without branching on it. Its output
  changes only in that it now reports a different value. Needs **disclosure** in the checkpoint.

Two refinements the first scan needed, both recorded because they changed the answer:

1. **A bare `\btier\b` matched 259 non-test files.** This repo also has build tiers, pricing
   tiers, provider-capability tiers and curriculum prose using the word, none of which can change
   when an *enrollment's* tier changes. A `tier` mention now counts only when the file also talks
   about enrollments. That took the list from 277 rows to 50.
2. **Comments were being classified as branching.** The first scan listed `config/env.ts`,
   `cohortService.ts` and `withdrawTestDemoRevenueAccounts.ts` on the strength of sentences like
   *"not just `enrollment_type='explorer'`"*. A comment cannot flip an outcome, and a
   "behaviour test per branching file" criterion is **unsatisfiable** for a file whose only
   mention is prose — so the criterion would have been quietly dropped for those files, which is
   exactly how a list stops meaning anything. Comments are now stripped before classification,
   which took branching from 31 to 28.

   **That fix then demoted a file that really does branch, and the correction matters more than
   the fix.** For `config/env.ts` and `withdrawTestDemoRevenueAccounts.ts` the comment was the
   *only* mention, so demotion was right. For **`cohortService.ts` the comment was only the first
   thing the regex matched** — the file also carries a real query filter at `:431`, in a form none
   of the branching rules recognised. So comment-stripping silently moved a genuine branching
   consumer into the reporting bucket, where it would never have been given a behaviour test. A
   rule was added for that form and the file is now row 29. Branching: 31 → 28 → **29**.

## REPORTING — 19 files

**`paymentSyncService.ts` is listed as REPORTING although it is a WRITER**, and the
mismatch is recorded rather than corrected. It writes both columns, but in raw SQL via a
`CASE WHEN :status = 'paid'` expression, which the generator does not read as a branch.
The classification is the scanner's, and the scanner is deliberately not being taught to
understand SQL `CASE` — that is the write-shape classification T203 failed three times
trying to build. What matters is that the file is in the enumeration at all, with a
determination saying what it really does; its coherence is proved behaviourally in
`services/__tests__/writerPairCoherence.test.ts`, not by its row here.

## A bug this scan had, recorded because it was the dangerous direction

The first comment-stripper matched block comments with a lazy dot-all regex, which cannot tell a
real block-comment opener from the same two characters inside a string or a regex literal. On
`server.ts` — 187 KB, full of SQL template literals — it swallowed **about 61% of the
non-whitespace** (149,436 characters down to roughly 58,660), taking the `enrollment_type` mention
with it, so **the file that creates both columns dropped out of the scan entirely.** The 149,436
and the disappearance both reproduce exactly; the post-strip figure is approximate because the
implementation that produced it no longer exists, and reconstructions land a character apart. Said
as approximate rather than quoted to the digit, because a precise-looking number nobody can
reproduce is worse than an honest range.

That is an **under-count**, which is strictly worse than a false positive here: the tripwire would
have reported clean while missing a consumer. Replaced with a per-line rule that treats a line as
a comment only when its first non-space characters say so, which cannot run away past its own
line, and which keeps the code half of a trailing comment — so the error, when it happens, is
over-counting. Both directions are covered by tests in
`backend/src/services/__tests__/freeAccountConsumers.test.ts`.

## What this enumeration does NOT claim

- It does not claim the frontend is covered. It scans `backend/src` only. Frontend consumers of
  `tier` and `is_explorer` are T202b's and T212's concern.
- It does not claim to find consumers that read these columns through a view, a cached JSON blob,
  or a string built at runtime. A regex over source cannot see those, and saying so is the
  difference between a bounded check and a false guarantee.
- **It does not see a consumer that reads a DERIVED value instead of the column**, and this is the
  most consequential limitation, because row 2's headline effect is implemented in one of them.
  `contentEntitlement.isFreePreviewTier` is the function that reads `enrollment_type`; the
  **truncation itself** lives in `services/timeline/timelineService.ts`, where
  `const cards = isFreeTier ? allCards.filter((c) => c.week === 0) : allCards;` is what actually
  removes weeks 1–12. Two more read the derived flag rather than the column:
  `services/timeline/todayAnchoredSources.ts` (`feed.is_explorer === true`) and
  `controllers/participantController.ts` (`is_explorer` in the response). None of the three
  contains either column name, so no regex over these two column names can find them, however
  good its rules are. **T202b must put the Week-0 behaviour test where the truncation is**, not
  only where the predicate is.
- **It recognises only the comparison forms it has rules for**, which is the limitation that
  actually bit this document. The rules cover `x === 'literal'`, `key: 'literal'`, the SQL
  comparison forms, and — added after the miss — Sequelize operator objects of the shape
  `key: { [Op.…]: … }`. A filter expressed some other way would be classified reporting-only and
  would not be given a behaviour test. Searched exhaustively for the remaining forms at the time
  of writing: no `IN`, `NOT IN`, `LIKE` or `CASE WHEN` usage on either column anywhere in
  `backend/src`, and the only operator-object or array occurrences are the dashboard filter cited
  below plus three column definitions. **This is a known blind spot, not a solved problem** — the
  completeness tripwire proves a file is *listed*, never that it is in the right bucket.
- It does not measure production. No row count, no flag value, no claim about how many real
  accounts are in either population — this phase takes no production read before T216.
